headline: Resource competition sets weights and thresholds in molecular perceptron circuits
label: Genetic Circuit Design Principles
summary: Recent preprints and a hardware p-computer demonstration extend perceptron-like molecular computing to classification, regression, and docking.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of simple neural-network abstractions to describe and design molecular computation. Two preprints model protein and CRISPR-based circuits as perceptron-like elements, and both treat resource competition as an explicit variable. Ribosome competition rescales the effective weights of sequestration-based protein neural networks, while resource competition in dCas9 perceptrons preserves classification boundaries and regression thresholds. What is new is the explicit treatment of shared translational and molecular resources as determinants of weights and thresholds. The published study extends this probabilistic framing to hardware, using a Gaussian-RNG p-bit prototype with RRAM compute-in-memory to solve a 42-node molecular docking problem.
